chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from al-Hasan ibn Sahl, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mihran, who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and on his finger was a ring with a turquoise stone, engraved with 'Allah al-Malik'. I kept looking at it, so he said: 'What is the matter with you, that you keep looking at it?' I said: 'It has reached me that there was for Ali, Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), a ring with a turquoise stone, engraved with 'Allah al-Malik'.'

He said: 'Do you recognize it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'This is it. Do you know the reason for it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'This is a stone that Jibra'il (peace be upon him) gifted to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gifted it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). Do you know its name?' I said: 'Turquoise.' He said: 'This is in Persian. So what is its name in Arabic?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'Its name is Al-Zafar.'

key_terms.الظَّفَرُ: Al-Zafar (Victory, the Arabic name of the stone)
key_terms.اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ: Allah the King (engraving on the ring)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and significance of the turquoise ring worn by the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual lineage of Imam Musa al-Kazim’s turban ring, tracing its origin to a gift from Jibra’il to the Prophet and then to Imam Ali, thereby establishing a chain of sacred authority (*isnad*) within the Ahl al-Bayt. The identification of the stone as 'Al-Zafar' (Victory) underscores the theological significance of material objects in Shia tradition as vessels of divine blessing (*barakah*) and victory, connecting the Imam’s physical presence to the prophetic era. This narrative reinforces the concept of *Tawassul* through the Imams' possessions, illustrating how their attributes reflect the continuity of divine guidance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Al Hassan Bin Sahl, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Mihran who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> finger was a ring with a stone of turquoise with an engraving: ‘اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ’ “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”. So I deliberated looking at it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with you, deliberately looking at it?’ So I said, ‘It has reached me that there was for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> a ring with a stone of turquoise with an engraving: “Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the King”’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you recognise it?’ I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is it. Do you know what is the reason for it?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a stone gifted by Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> gifted it to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>. Do you know what it’s name is?’ I said, ‘Turquoise’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is in Persian. So what is its name in Arabic?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its name is Al-Zafar’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from al-Hassan ibn Sahl from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once visited abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and on his finger was a ring with a stone which was turquoise with an engraving that said, ’Allah is the owner’. I continued looking on it and he (the Imam) asked, ’Why do you continue looking at it?’ I replied, ‘I have received information that Ali, ’Amir al-Mu’minin had a ring which had a stone of turquoise and its engraving said, “Allah is the owner”.’

He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you recognize it?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not recognize it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is that ring; do you know what is the reason?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is a stone which Jibril gave as a gift to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and the Messenger of Allah gave it as a gift to ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Do you know what its name is?’ I replied, ‘It is Firozaj (turquoise).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘That is in al-Farsiyah. What is its name in Arabic?’ I replied, ‘I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Its name is al-Zafar (victory).”’
